question_text: Find the vertex, focus, equation of the directrix and axis of the parabola y² = 16x.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a
steps.why: Comparing the given equation to the standard form y² = 4ax is the one step needed before every one of the four quantities asked for can be read off.
common_mistakes: Reading a = 16 instead of dividing by 4 to get a = 4.
steps.memory_tip: Compare to y² = 4ax first — every other answer in this question is read straight off a.

steps.label: State the vertex, focus, directrix and axis
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for all four answers together — losing any one of the four costs part of this mark.
lines: (iii) Equation of the directrix: x = −a ⇒ x + 4 = 0
steps.why: For the standard form y² = 4ax the vertex is always the origin, the focus and directrix sit at ±a on the x-axis, and the axis is the x-axis itself — all four facts follow from the single number a found in step 1.
common_mistakes: Writing the directrix as x = a instead of x = −a.
Giving the axis as x = 0 instead of y = 0.
steps.memory_tip: For y² = 4ax: vertex at the origin, focus at (a,0), directrix at x = −a, axis is the x-axis itself (y = 0).

insider_note: All four parts are asked in one question worth two marks total, so each part needs to be stated cleanly and briefly rather than derived at length.
